rationale: Evidence from iteration 5 (kd 0.1 to 0.2, all else as iteration 3/4): score 41.1832, the best raced so far. Oval steering_oscillation fell only from 0.1133 to 0.111, far above the 0.09 threshold in the Evaluator's rule (a), so raising kd did not remove the oscillation. Oval max_error was 0.0613 and s-bend/slalom max_error was 0.0612/0.0611. The s-bend and slalom oscillation rose only slightly (0.0668 and 0.0633), below the 0.08 rollback trigger, and progress did not fall (s-bend 0.0409, slalom 0.035), so kd 0.2 stays. Every run still ends off_track with progress of only 0.04 on the s-bend and slalom. The robot leaves the line early and at a near-constant point, with max_error pinned at about 0.061 regardless of kp, ki or kd. Across iterations 3 to 5, changing kp (3.0 to 2.5), ki (0.3 to 0.5) and kd (0.1 to 0.2) moved the score by under 0.5 in total. That points to a fixed bias or a speed-limited excursion, not a gain problem. The most plausible cause is slip and outward drift at base_speed 1.4, which the Evaluator also flagged. I change one group: controller.base_speed from 1.4 to 1.2, keeping kp 2.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.2 and the geometry unchanged. Expected result, not measured: lower speed reduces outward drift in the bends, so s-bend and slalom progress rises above 0.041 and 0.035 and max_error falls below 0.061. Finishing is still unlikely within 3 s, so the time term may fall, but progress gains should outweigh that. Risk: if progress does not improve, the bias is in the sensors or the mismatch, and the next test should be a wider outer sensor set or the noise check. Hypotheses for the next race: (1) if progress rises and max_error falls, speed-driven slip was the limit; (2) if max_error stays at about 0.061 on all tracks with unchanged progress, the error is a sensor or motor-mismatch bias, so test sensor geometry next. Measurements requested: all metrics plus noise_robustness, to separate sensor noise from fixed bias.
